summary: DashboardService.list_as_of correctly orchestrates list_active_all + sum_deltas_by_source_type + opening/closing_balance, asserts FORMULA-001, and sorts in Python by (design_name, grade_code). All 7 load-bearing properties verified; no SQL composition, no scope creep, no security issues.
decisions_consulted: DS-002 (advisory-lock-first writes — write-path concern, not relevant to this read-only service)
DS-003 (running_balance materialization — implementation calls opening/closing primitives which are O(1) latest_as_of lookups)
DS-004 (opening = closing of prev day — encapsulated in domain.stock.opening_balance; service does NOT re-derive)
DS-015 (perf target p95 < 500ms — single GROUP BY + O(N) latest_as_of pattern preserves the budget)
DS-016 (single GROUP BY for dashboard — implementation invokes sum_deltas_by_source_type exactly once)

Line 50: month_first = as_of_date.replace(day=1). Passed as month_start to the aggregate query AND to opening_balance (which itself subtracts 1 day per DS-004).

Service accesses pair.design.design_name, pair.design.size, pair.grade.grade_code (lines 90-93) — all served from the already-joined row. No explicit selectinload/joinedload needed; no N+1.

All 5 steps in the LLD function description are present in order: (1) month_first derivation, (2) list_active_all, (3) single GROUP BY via sum_deltas_by_source_type, (4) per-pair opening/closing + aggregate dict lookup with default-0 missing-key handling, (5) invariant assert, plus final sort. Plan.json output_files[] matches the single file written.

Exports: DashboardService (matches LLD interfaces.exports). Imports match depends_on[]: src.domain.stock (opening_balance, closing_balance), src.infrastructure.db.repositories.ledger_aggregates (LedgerAggregatesRepository), src.infrastructure.db.repositories.master (DesignGradeMapRepository), src.presentation.schemas.dashboard (DashboardRow). All imported symbols are used. Method signatures of called functions match: sum_deltas_by_source_type(month_start, as_of_date) returns Row objects with .design_id/.grade_id/.inward_sum/.outward_sum/.adjust_sum (verified against ledger_aggregates.py:46-74); opening_balance/closing_balance take (session, design_id, grade_id, date) returning int (verified against stock.py:123-143); list_active_all() returns list[DesignGradeMapModel] (verified against master.py:59-70). DashboardRow constructor receives all 10 fields it declares (dashboard.py:1-16).

TC-115 (3 pairs, all 10 fields populated) — satisfied; all 10 fields constructed from pair + mov + opening + closing. TC-116 (zero active pairs) — list_active_all returns [], outer loop is no-op, rows=[] returned (empty list, not error). TC-118 (opening = closing prev-day) — delegated to opening_balance which calls closing_balance(month_first - 1 day) per DS-004. TC-119 (inward/outward/adjust from monthly aggregates) — agg_by_key built from sum_deltas_by_source_type Row tuples, missing keys default to {0,0,0}. TC-120 (closing = latest_as_of) — delegated to closing_balance. TC-121 (no movements in window) — agg_by_key.get(key, {0,0,0}) yields zeros; opening + 0 - 0 + 0 == closing holds because no in-window movement means closing == opening. TC-122 (perf p95 < 500ms) — architecture: 1 query for pairs + 1 GROUP BY + 2 indexed lookups per pair = under budget for 6 pairs. TC-127 (movement default 0) — explicit default dict in .get fallback. TC-128 (AssertionError on invariant) — bare assert with diagnostic message. TC-129 (sort by design_name, grade_code) — explicit final sort. TC-156 (carry-forward through month boundary) — opening_balance returns closing of month-N last day; this is automatic correct behaviour since closing_balance reads materialized running_balance which is recomputed by _recompute_forward on back-dated insertion.

No user-controlled string is concatenated into a query (no SQL composition at all in this file). as_of_date is a datetime.date object — type-safety enforced by Python; .replace(day=1) is a method call on a date, not a string operation. No secrets, no logging of sensitive values, no eval/exec. Assertion message includes only int IDs and int balances — no PII. No external I/O, no auth concerns (per DS-005 V1 has no auth). Note: assert is correctly used as a correctness invariant (DS-016 documents this as a hard property), not a defensive check that could be stripped by -O — and even if stripped, downstream consumers see corrupt data only if the ledger is already corrupt, which is a separate (and prevented) class of bug.

File contains exactly one class with one public method plus __init__. No additional helpers, no extra exports, no modifications to do_not_touch files (domain/stock.py, repositories/*, schemas/dashboard.py — all untouched per plan). No router code, no DI factory (correctly left to T-062 + dependencies.py modification). No test file authored. No SQL in service. No re-derivation of DS-003/DS-004 logic. The implementation is the minimum surface area required to satisfy the plan.
